newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU oil figures expected to show growing stockpiles.
newsitem.headline: EU oil figures expected to show growing stockpiles.

text.p: European oil inventory figures, to be released on Tuesday, are expected to show a rising stockpile of both crude and oil products last month, analysts said.
"The underlying position will have continued to ease (in February)," said Geoff Pyne, oil analyst at Swiss bank UBS.

Despite onset of spring, many analysts were still looking closest at the middle distillate figures. All those questioned said they expected the mild February weather to have resulted in an even higher year-on-year surplus by the end of the month.

"We expect (middle distillate stocks) to have taken a fairly considerable step upwards...At the end of January (stocks) were already above levels in January 1996. At the end of February, we expect them to be even higher," said Colin Birch, principal consultant at Purvin and Gertz in London.

February 1996 brought on a cold snap which drove prices to what were then three-year highs and premiums to levels unmatched since the 1991 Gulf War, eating into stocks. This season, temperatures throughout most of western Europe have averaged above zero degrees Celsius.
Certain Mediterranean refineries cut runs at the start of February, but those in northern Europe resisted until last week when a number in ARA reduced output by around 10 percent.

"The cutbacks only really seem to have taken effect in March. In February, especially following a cold January, (refineries) were running at full speed," said Peter Bogin, associate director at Cambridge Energy Research Associates in Paris.
Despite the high refinery throughput, crude oil stocks may also have risen with the arrival of an increasing number of cargoes.
Gasoline stocks are also expected to have risen, although they may well remain below year-ago levels.
